summary: Attacked part 2 of the Number fields and class field theory area — GlobalNumberFields, GlobalQuadraticForms, LocalFieldsRamification, Multiquadratic, NumberFieldArithmetic, PolynomialGaloisGroups and QuadraticFormInvariants, 65 stages. One finding, medium: all seven roadmaps declare an empty prerequisites list while their own prose states three dependencies among them, one of them at declaration level, and 76 per cent of atlas roadmaps do use that field. The library-boundary head is clean: the global quadratic-form theory the area plans — Hasse-Minkowski, the Hasse invariant, Witt consequences, the Hilbert symbol — is genuinely absent from Mathlib, so the roadmap that barely mentions the library is not neglecting it but has little to consume.
checked: Every stage of all seven roadmaps: QuadraticFormInvariants 18, GlobalNumberFields 12, GlobalQuadraticForms 10, NumberFieldArithmetic 8, PolynomialGaloisGroups 8, LocalFieldsRamification 5, Multiquadratic 4 — 65 in all.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the 43 papers this session has reviewed routes to any of these seven roadmaps. I computed entanglement across every available area red team before choosing.

The stage-level graph and status, calibrated against the atlas. All 65 stages have empty `requires` and status 'unknown'; atlas-wide those are 669 of 1962 (34 per cent) and 656 of 1962 (33 per cent). Within norms, and not the finding.

Sibling citations, with the direction of each established from the sentence rather than assumed — the check that matters, since a citation can equally name a consumer. Four pairs carry citations. Three run backwards and are genuine dependencies: QuadraticFormInvariants on LocalFieldsRamification ('The general arithmetic of a nonarchimedean local field belongs to the [local-fields-ramification roadmap], and this sublayer consumes it'); NumberFieldArithmetic on LocalFieldsRamification ('[that roadmap] for the precise ValuativeExtension contract consumed below', and 'Every use of the local API of [the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap] is through this instance'); and GlobalNumberFields on NumberFieldArithmetic, at declaration level ('Define idealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.idealsAway m.support').

The two citations that run forwards, and so are not dependencies: QuadraticFormInvariants naming GlobalQuadraticForms ('The resulting frozen declaration hilbertSymbol_productFormula is an export to GlobalQuadraticForms'), and LocalFieldsRamification naming NumberFieldArithmetic ('This is a local theorem: [the Number-Field Arithmetic roadmap] consumes it only after passing to a completion'). The latter matters because it resolves what looks like a mutual dependency between those two roadmaps into supplier and consumer, so there is no cycle.

Roadmap-level prerequisites atlas-wide, which is what turns the empty lists from a convention into a finding: 161 of 211 atlas roadmaps (76 per cent) declare at least one prerequisite, and 0 of these 7 do. The sibling Representation theory area shows the field is used where dependencies exist — CharacterTheory declares three, SpinRepresentations three, QuiverRepresentations, LieHighestWeight and CompactGroups two each.

The library boundary, the head that produced the model-theory area's sharpest finding. Mathlib engagement across the seven runs from 101 mentions (NumberFieldArithmetic) and 77 (PolynomialGaloisGroups) down to 2 (GlobalQuadraticForms, Multiquadratic), and the low end looked like a roadmap planning without checking the library. It is not: GlobalQuadraticForms plans places and completions, archimedean signatures, finite-place invariants, Hasse-Minkowski isotropy, representation and isometry, and global classification with Witt consequences, and Mathlib has none of that global theory. Searching the pinned tree, HasseMinkowski, hasseInvariant, WittGroup/WittRing and hilbertSymbol each return zero files, against 42 files for QuadraticForm and 5 mentioning isotropy. So the global layer is correctly planned and the low mention count reflects little to consume rather than neglect.

That QuadraticFormInvariants' references to a Hilbert symbol are consistent with that absence: it names ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductFormula and exports hilbertSymbol_productFormula, which are Tau Ceti and sibling-roadmap declarations rather than Mathlib ones, matching the zero hits for hilbertSymbol in the library.

Whether any paper in the blueprint routes to these seven roadmaps, which decides whether PROTOCOL section 17's omissions head has paper needs to test against. Checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files: 0 routes name any of the seven as their roadmap. A crude substring scan first suggested the opposite, returning 31 to 49 matching files per roadmap, but every match sits in a paper's `examined` record or prose — roadmaps considered as a destination and rejected — and none is a route. So the omissions head could be run only against the roadmaps' own targets, and this red team makes no claim about paper needs.

The calibration itself, rechecked after this red team shipped, because the first version of the finding leaned on it. The atlas-wide figure of 161 of 211 roadmaps (76 per cent) declaring a prerequisite is correct but decomposes sharply by origin: campaign-origin 147 of 151 (97 per cent), tauceti-origin 14 of 60 (23 per cent). All seven roadmaps here are tauceti-origin, so 0 of 7 is close to what that class predicts and the base-rate argument does not support a finding. The finding was re-grounded on evidence that does not depend on a population rate: the reciprocal `consumers` field is in active use by the very suppliers involved — LocalFieldsRamification lists six consumers, NumberFieldArithmetic one — and the roadmaps named in the area's own prose are absent from those lists, so the three relations are recorded on neither side.

Why the stage-level graph is empty here, established rather than assumed, since part 1 of this area answers it. The three campaign-origin roadmaps of part 1 carry all 38 of that part's stage `requires` edges and status `needs_source_decomposition`; its four tauceti-origin roadmaps carry 0 edges and status `unknown`, exactly as all seven of part 2 do. Empty stage edges and `unknown` status track a roadmap's origin, not the attention its area has received, which is why they are not a finding for this part.

findings.where: The prerequisites field of all seven area roadmaps in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/: GlobalNumberFields, GlobalQuadraticForms, LocalFieldsRamification, Multiquadratic, NumberFieldArithmetic, PolynomialGaloisGroups, QuadraticFormInvariants
findings.claim: All seven roadmaps declare prerequisites: [], and none of the three dependencies their own prose states is recorded on the supplier side either, so the atlas records this area as seven roadmaps with no build order. One dependency is at declaration level: GlobalNumberFields defines objects as reducible abbreviations of NumberFieldArithmetic declarations, so it cannot be elaborated before that roadmap exists. A design or build-order job reading the machine-readable fields gets the ordering wrong, and a worker starting GlobalNumberFields or QuadraticFormInvariants discovers the dependency only on reading the prose. What makes this an omission rather than a house style is that these roadmaps do maintain the reciprocal field: LocalFieldsRamification lists six consumers and NumberFieldArithmetic one, and the roadmaps named in the area's own prose are missing from those lists.
findings.evidence: Empty on the consumer side: each of the seven roadmap records in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ has prerequisites: []. Empty on the supplier side too, which is the heart of this finding. tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_LocalFieldsRamification.json has consumers: ['ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations', 'LanglandsParameterStacks', 'LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles', 'ReductiveGroupsPartII', 'RelativeFarguesFontaine', 'VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals'] — six entries, and neither QuadraticFormInvariants nor NumberFieldArithmetic is among them, although both say in prose that they consume it. tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_NumberFieldArithmetic.json has consumers: ['ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights'] and does not list GlobalNumberFields. So the field is in active use and these three relations are missing from it. The three dependencies, quoted from the roadmaps' own stage descriptions. (1) QuadraticFormInvariants, sublayer 6A, titled 'The local-field substrate, consumed': 'The general arithmetic of a nonarchimedean local field belongs to the [local-fields-ramification roadmap](../LocalFieldsRamification/README.md), and this sublayer consumes it. The normalized valuation is that roadmap's normalizedValuation...'. (2) NumberFieldArithmetic, Layer 5: '[the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap](../LocalFieldsRamification/README.md) for the precise ValuativeExtension contract consumed below', and separately 'Every use of the local API of [the Local Fields and Ramification roadmap] is through this instance'. (3) GlobalNumberFields: 'Define idealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.idealsAway m.support, and integralIdealsPrimeTo m as the reducible abbreviation of NumberFieldArithmetic.integralIdealsAway m.support'. Direction was established from each sentence rather than assumed: the two remaining citations run the other way and are correctly not dependencies — 'is an export to GlobalQuadraticForms', and 'This is a local theorem: [the Number-Field Arithmetic roadmap] consumes it only after passing to a completion', the latter resolving the apparent mutual dependency between LocalFieldsRamification and NumberFieldArithmetic into supplier and consumer, with no cycle. Calibration, stated precisely because a cruder version of it would mislead: 161 of 211 atlas roadmaps (76 per cent) declare at least one prerequisite, but that rate decomposes sharply by origin — campaign-origin roadmaps 147 of 151 (97 per cent), tauceti-origin roadmaps only 14 of 60 (23 per cent). All seven of these are tauceti-origin, so against their own comparison class an empty prerequisites list is not by itself anomalous, and this finding does not rest on the base rate. It rests on the three documented relations being absent from both the prerequisites and the consumers fields while those roadmaps populate consumers with other entries.
findings.fix: Record the three stated relations. On the consumer side: QuadraticFormInvariants and NumberFieldArithmetic each gain tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification in prerequisites, and GlobalNumberFields gains tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic. On the supplier side, which is the fix that fits these roadmaps' existing practice: add QuadraticFormInvariants and NumberFieldArithmetic to LocalFieldsRamification's consumers list, and GlobalNumberFields to NumberFieldArithmetic's. Either side alone removes the gap for a consumer that reads both fields; doing both keeps them reciprocal, as they already are for the seven relations these two roadmaps do record. This introduces no cycle, because LocalFieldsRamification's only citation of NumberFieldArithmetic names it as a consumer. Leave GlobalQuadraticForms, Multiquadratic and PolynomialGaloisGroups as they are unless their documents state a dependency this red team did not find.
